correctness.rationale: Heawood incidence graph is the 14-vertex bipartite Fano graph, (i-j) mod 7 in {0,1,3}; induced subgraph forest predicate is acyclicity and maximum internal degree d. Degree bound d=0,1,2,3 exhausts the filtration because the graph is cubic. Independently enumerated all 2^14 vertex masks using connected-component edge-count identity |E|=|V|-c, giving nonempty face counts 457,2256,8654,12791. For each d reconstructed coordinate-toggle matching and verified every oriented Hasse-cover DAG by full topological visit: cover counts 1568,10150,50764,81634, all visits equal faces; pair counts 225,1121,4326,6391; critical counts respectively {0:1,3:6}, {0:1,5:13}, {0:1,6:1}, {0:1,8:8}. Therefore genuine integral CW homotopy wedges ∨6 S3, ∨13 S5, S6, ∨8 S8, since attaching to only a 0-skeleton is null. Strict successive homology maps vanish because occupied degrees do not coincide; integral barcode is isolated intervals by stage, and stage 3 persists identically onward. No inference of integral homotopy from mere mod2 ranks.
residual_risks: Finite canonical 14-vertex Heawood only; nonequivariant integral homotopy; no general cubic/incidence graph theorem. d=0 wedge6 S3 previously known.

value.rationale: Heawood is the smallest projective-plane incidence graph and a natural cubic girth-six test case. Giving every induced-forest degree stage as an integral wedge of spheres via explicit acyclic matchings is a natural complete classification, useful for comparison with more general incidence graphs; persistence is a faithful corollary, not falsely advertised as independent novelty.
residual_risks: A complete finite case need not generalize to higher projective planes and was not shown to do so.
